newsitem.title: USA: USDA tracking EU subsidies, will discuss - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: USDA tracking EU subsidies, will discuss - Glickman.

text.p: The United States is "tracking" the wheat export subsidies offered by the European Union and will make them a topic of a mid-level meeting next week in Brussels, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday.
"We are tracking that," Glickman told reporters before announcing that his trade adviser, Paul Drazek, would go to Brussels next week for agricultural trade discussions.
Drazek said export subsidies would be among the topics in meetings with EU agriculture commissioner Franz Fischler's chief of staff.
EU export subsidies have more or less followed the rise and fall in world wheat prices, Drazek said, but added the issue was how much the subsidies were being adjusted.

Last week, EU officials boosted their subsidies and created the possibility, analysts said, of undercutting U.S. prices, despite repeated vows to do no more than match world prices. A USDA official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said U.S. wheat exports remained strong and supplies relatively tight.
Another key issue for U.S.-EU resolution is so-called veterinary equivalency standards that are important to meat exports.
Drazek said it was important to resolve the issue before year's end, when a temporary settlement would expire. More than $500 million a year in U.S. meat exports was involved.
Also on the agenda, he said, would be the issue of U.S. rice exports to Europe.
The meetings would follow up a dinner meeting earlier this month between Fischler and Glickman in Rome.
"We expect to be able to resolve (the equivalency issue) by the end of this year," Drazek said. "It's certainly do-able and when things are do-able, they usually get done."

It still appeared likely, Drazek said, that the EU would decide by the end of December whether to allow sale of a genetically modified corn that repels the corn borer, a major pest. The United States expects eventual EU approval of the product.
